paragraphs: Detecting unusual nodes in a graph usually requires training a model for that particular dataset. ARC investigates a more reusable approach: a single detector that can work across graph datasets. At prediction time, it uses a few examples of normal nodes to understand the target dataset, without retraining or fine-tuning its parameters.

The architecture separates this task into three parts. A feature-alignment module puts different datasets into a shared representation that remains sensitive to anomalies. A graph encoder then produces node representations using differences between a node and its neighbors. Finally, a cross-attention module compares the resulting information with the supplied normal examples to assign anomaly scores.

The normal examples provide context about what counts as ordinary in the new graph. This allows dataset-specific information to influence predictions without a new training run. Experiments across benchmarks from several domains report advantages in detection performance, efficiency, and generalization, supporting ARC as an approach to reusable graph anomaly detection.
neurips-2024-arc-a-generalist-graph-anom.tldr: ARC uses a few normal examples to detect graph anomalies across datasets without target-specific retraining.

paragraphs: A model's uncertainty can serve several purposes: deciding when to withhold a prediction, detecting unfamiliar inputs, or estimating ambiguity inherent in the data. Uncertainty disentanglement asks for something more specific than an overall confidence score. It seeks separate estimators, each responding to only one source of uncertainty.

This paper introduces a benchmark for testing whether existing methods achieve that separation in practice. The authors reimplement a broad selection of Bayesian, evidential, and deterministic uncertainty estimators and evaluate them across multiple uncertainty tasks on ImageNet. This shared evaluation makes it possible to compare both task performance and whether pairs of estimators actually isolate different uncertainty sources.

Among the approaches evaluated, none produces successfully disentangled estimator pairs in practice. Specialized uncertainty tasks also prove harder than general predictive uncertainty tasks, where performance appears to be leveling off. The findings support choosing estimators according to the particular task, while identifying a remaining gap between theoretical approaches to separating uncertainty and the behavior observed in this benchmark.
neurips-2024-benchmarking-uncertainty-di.tldr: An ImageNet benchmark finds that evaluated uncertainty methods do not successfully separate uncertainty sources in practice.

paragraphs: Learning from a small labeled dataset becomes particularly difficult when some classes have many examples and others have very few. Adding unlabeled data can help, but its class frequencies may differ from those of the labeled examples. Methods that depend heavily on model-generated labels must therefore deal with both unreliable predictions and mismatched distributions.

The paper develops a probabilistic framework that connects several existing approaches to learning with uneven class frequencies. It derives a class-balanced contrastive objective through Gaussian kernel density estimation, linking the learned representation to class balancing. Continuous Contrastive Learning, or CCL, extends this framework to unlabeled examples using reliable, smoothed pseudo-labels.

CCL progressively estimates the underlying label distribution and adjusts its alignment with model predictions. This explicitly addresses the possibility that unlabeled data has a different class distribution. Across experiments with varying unlabeled distributions, the method consistently outperforms the compared state-of-the-art approaches, including a reported improvement exceeding 4% on ImageNet-127. The results support jointly addressing representation learning, pseudo-label quality, and distribution mismatch.
neurips-2024-continuous-contrastive-lear.tldr: CCL combines class-balanced contrastive learning with smoothed pseudo-labels and distribution estimation to improve long-tailed semi-supervised recognition.

paragraphs: Cyber threat intelligence uses knowledge about threats to help people understand and mitigate security risks. Language models could support this work, but their usefulness depends on reliable, accurate answers rather than plausible-looking mistakes. The paper argues that general language-model benchmarks do not adequately assess the practical demands of this particular field.

CTIBench supplies a dedicated evaluation benchmark containing multiple datasets for cyber threat intelligence tasks. Its focus is the knowledge models have acquired about the cyber-threat landscape and how that knowledge performs in applied CTI settings. This gives researchers a way to examine domain-specific capabilities instead of inferring them from performance on unrelated general evaluations.

The authors evaluate several state-of-the-art models and use the results to identify strengths and weaknesses within CTI. The stated contribution is a clearer basis for assessing model capabilities in this domain. By organizing evaluation around CTI applications, the benchmark makes reliability concerns more directly testable and helps distinguish broad language ability from performance on the security tasks being assessed.
neurips-2024-ctibench-a-benchmark-for-ev.tldr: CTIBench evaluates language models on cyber threat intelligence tasks to reveal domain-specific strengths and weaknesses.

paragraphs: As generated images become more realistic and widespread online, datasets collected from the internet may increasingly mix real and synthetic content. This paper examines what that mixture means for online continual learning, where models keep learning as data arrives. Its concern is whether synthetic contamination interferes with the training of existing methods.

The authors experimentally investigate contaminated datasets and find that they can hinder online continual learning. They then introduce Entropy Selection with Real-synthetic similarity Maximization, or ESRM, to reduce the resulting deterioration. The approach combines an entropy-based selection component with an objective that encourages similarity between real and synthetic data.

Experiments show that ESRM can substantially alleviate the performance loss, with particularly strong benefits when contamination is severe. The finding is specific to the investigated learning setting: synthetic images can create a training problem, and a method designed around their presence can lessen it. This makes dataset composition an explicit part of the continual-learning problem rather than assuming that incoming image data is uniformly suitable for training.
neurips-2024-dealing-with-synthetic-data.tldr: ESRM reduces the performance deterioration that synthetic-image contamination can cause in online continual learning.

paragraphs: Training labels supplied by people can contain mistakes, especially when the categories are visually difficult to distinguish. The dopanim dataset turns this difficulty into a benchmark by collecting images of animals that resemble one another. It contains about 15,750 images across 15 classes, together with ground-truth labels for evaluating learning methods.

For approximately 10,500 images, 20 people supplied more than 52,000 annotations, with an overall accuracy of about 67%. The annotations include human-estimated likelihoods, allowing the data to express uncertainty beyond a single class choice. Information about annotators is also included, providing additional material for methods that learn from multiple people's judgments.

The authors benchmark established multi-annotator learning methods on seven dataset variants. They also describe uses such as learning from richer labels and active learning. The dataset's value comes from combining a difficult recognition task with actual human annotation behavior. Its public codebase supports reproducing the reported results and emulating the collection process, making the evaluation easier to inspect and repeat.
neurips-2024-dopanim-a-dataset-of-doppel.tldr: dopanim benchmarks learning from noisy human judgments using visually similar animals, likelihood annotations, and annotator metadata.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning trains an agent from an existing dataset. A central difficulty is that the agent may assign overly optimistic values to actions poorly represented in that data. Avoiding all actions outside the dataset can limit this problem, but the paper argues that modest generalization can improve performance under certain conditions.

Doubly Mild Generalization, or DMG, controls two distinct parts of that process. First, it considers actions in a close neighborhood of recorded actions when seeking high predicted value. Second, it limits how generalization errors spread through bootstrapping, where value estimates help construct subsequent learning targets. This second control aims to contain errors while preserving useful reinforcement-learning signals.

The theoretical improvement over the best in-sample policy applies in an oracle generalization scenario. Under worst-case generalization, the analysis instead provides control over value overestimation and a lower performance bound. Experiments report state-of-the-art results on Gym-MuJoCo locomotion and AntMaze tasks. The method also supports moving from offline training to online learning, with strong reported fine-tuning performance.
neurips-2024-doubly-mild-generalization-.tldr: DMG improves offline reinforcement learning by controlling both nearby action generalization and the propagation of its errors.

paragraphs: If people can reliably supervise easier problems but struggle with harder ones, can that easier supervision still improve a model's harder reasoning? This paper studies that question using mathematical problems at different difficulty levels. Its central idea is to transfer an evaluator's judgment from easier tasks to harder tasks, then use those judgments to improve generated solutions.

The approach first trains process-supervised reward models on easy problems. These evaluators score candidate solutions to harder problems, providing a signal for either reranking generated answers or training the generator with reinforcement learning. The important connection is that an evaluator's ability to generalize can support the generator's own improvement across difficulty levels.

Using human supervision only on easy problems, the reported 7-billion-parameter reinforcement-learning model reaches 34.0% accuracy on MATH500. A 34-billion-parameter model using reranking over 1,024 candidates reaches 52.5%. These results support easy-to-hard transfer in the studied reasoning setting and suggest a possible route to extending supervision beyond the problems people directly annotate.
neurips-2024-easy-to-hard-generalization.tldr: Reward models trained on easier math problems can guide reranking or reinforcement learning on harder problems.

paragraphs: Cross-modal hashing creates compact codes for retrieving related items across different data types. Missing labels make it difficult to tell which item pairs truly match. The paper uses vision-language knowledge to recover those labels, while observing that direct zero-shot predictions from models such as CLIP are not sufficient for the task.

PCRIL learns to judge how completely a label set describes an example. It considers subsets of known positive labels and constructs contrasting prompts by deleting, adding, or replacing labels. This supervision helps address the limited, uneven label combinations in training data. A greedy tree search then progressively identifies promising unknown labels and searches for additional relevant ones.

For cases with many unknown labels or inadequate negative-pair supervision, the method adds mixup using samples with complementary unknown labels and random flipping for negative labels. Experiments report an average 12% improvement in mean average precision over the current state of the art across the tested datasets. The results support improving retrieval by actively reconstructing incomplete supervision.
neurips-2024-exploiting-descriptive-comp.tldr: PCRIL learns label-set completeness and searches for missing labels to improve cross-modal retrieval with incomplete supervision.

paragraphs: Vision state space models process image tokens with linear computational complexity, but they can still benefit from removing less informative tokens. This paper investigates that opportunity and finds that pruning techniques developed for vision transformers transfer poorly, even after extensive fine-tuning. The authors trace the problem to disruption of the sequential positions used by state space computation.

Their method adapts pruning to that structure. A hidden-state alignment mechanism accounts for pruning and stabilizes the neighborhood of the tokens that remain. A separate importance measure, designed for state space models, determines which tokens to remove. Together, these components address both token selection and the effect of removal on subsequent computation.

The implementation also includes practical acceleration, producing actual speedups alongside reduced operation counts. Across several tasks, experiments report substantial computational reductions with little performance impact. In one stated result, pruned PlainMamba-L3 achieves 81.7% ImageNet accuracy with 41.6% fewer floating-point operations. The study shows why efficiency techniques need to respect the sequence-processing behavior of the architecture receiving them.
neurips-2024-exploring-token-pruning-in-.tldr: Architecture-aware token pruning reduces vision state space model computation while preserving the sequential structure needed for strong performance.

paragraphs: Observational data can leave a causal effect unresolved when unmeasured factors influence the variables involved. Direct experiments may resolve that difficulty, but intervening on the variable of interest can be expensive or infeasible. Proxy experiments offer another route: intervene on cheaper variables that still allow the desired causal effect to be identified.

The paper studies how to choose such experiments at minimum cost. Earlier work established that this design problem is NP-complete and supplied an algorithm that could require exponentially many difficult subproblems in the worst case. The new contribution is a set of reformulations that make substantially more efficient solution algorithms possible.

Extensive simulations provide evidence for the improved computational efficiency. The paper also examines experiment design for identifying effects through valid adjustment sets, connecting intervention choices with another route to causal identification. The practical significance is better computational handling of a difficult design problem: finding affordable experiments that supply the information needed to identify a particular effect.
neurips-2024-fast-proxy-experiment-desig.tldr: New reformulations make it faster to design low-cost proxy experiments that identify a desired causal effect.

paragraphs: An agent that keeps learning over its lifetime can become less able to adapt as a consequence of its earlier training. This loss of plasticity means that past progress can obstruct learning on new tasks. Existing remedies such as regularization and resetting can help, but they depend on carefully chosen settings that may need to change with the environment.

TRAC addresses the problem at the optimizer level. Built from the theory of online convex optimization, it is presented as parameter-free: it requires neither tuning nor advance knowledge of distribution shifts. This targets a practical difficulty of lifelong learning, where the changes an agent will encounter may be unknown when training begins.

Experiments on Procgen, Atari, and Gym Control show TRAC mitigating plasticity loss and adapting rapidly to challenging shifts. These are empirical findings in reinforcement-learning problems that are both nonconvex and changing over time, despite the optimizer's theoretical roots in convex optimization. The results support the usefulness of this optimizer design beyond the setting that originally motivates its theory.
neurips-2024-fast-trac-a-parameter-free-.tldr: TRAC is a tuning-free optimizer that empirically helps lifelong reinforcement-learning agents retain adaptability through distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Continual generalized category discovery asks a model to discover new classes while continuing to recognize old ones. After initial training on labeled examples, it receives unlabeled data containing both familiar and unfamiliar classes. This paper studies an extended setting with more new classes over a longer period and no storage of past-class samples.

The authors identify prediction bias and hardness bias as obstacles to balancing discovery and retention. Happy addresses prediction bias with clustering-guided initialization and soft entropy regularization. These components provide useful starting features and encourage appropriate probabilities for new classes, improving their clustering. Hardness-aware prototype sampling addresses forgetting, with particular attention to difficult previously learned classes.

The framework therefore tackles two sides of the same learning conflict: making room for new categories and maintaining distinctions already learned. Experiments across several datasets report strong performance, including a 7.5% overall gain on ImageNet-100. The findings support the proposed bias-reduction mechanisms in a setting where retaining old examples is unavailable as a way to preserve earlier knowledge.
neurips-2024-happy-a-debiased-learning-f.tldr: Happy reduces prediction and hardness biases to discover new classes from unlabeled data while limiting forgetting without storing past samples.

paragraphs: Fully homomorphic encryption allows neural-network training computations to operate on encrypted data, but repeated forward and backward passes are expensive. Removing redundant training examples could reduce that work. The complication is that deciding which encrypted examples to remove can itself require costly encrypted computations, making ordinary data-pruning methods difficult to apply.

HEPrune introduces a pruning protocol and algorithms designed for encrypted computation, covering settings with and without client assistance. It also addresses a second obstacle: deleting individual samples may leave empty spaces inside ciphertexts without eliminating the ciphertext computations. Sample removal alone can therefore fail to translate into the expected training savings.

The method adds ciphertext-wise pruning to reduce the number of ciphertexts processed, a step the authors describe as preserving accuracy. For the overall system, experiments report a 16-fold speedup over prior work with a 0.6% accuracy drop. The contribution connects selecting less training data with actually reducing the encrypted workload, which is necessary for pruning to deliver useful computational gains.
neurips-2024-heprune-fast-private-traini.tldr: HEPrune accelerates encrypted neural-network training by pruning both redundant samples and the ciphertext computations that contain them.

paragraphs: Paying for generated text by token count can reward quantity without ensuring that the provider uses a capable model. Because inference happens internally, a provider may quietly choose a cheaper model to reduce costs. The paper frames this as an incentive problem and studies contracts that base payment on automated evaluations of output quality.

The framework models a customer and a text-generating agent whose inference has a cost. A central difficulty is that the customer may not know that internal cost. The authors introduce cost-robust contracts for this situation and characterize optimal contracts through a correspondence with optimal composite hypothesis tests in statistics.

This connection turns statistical distinctions between output distributions into a way to reason about payment rules. The authors construct contracts for multiple objectives and language-model evaluation benchmarks. Empirically, the cost-robust contracts incur only a marginal increase in objective value relative to cost-aware versions. The result suggests that useful performance incentives can be designed even when the agent's inference costs are unknown.
neurips-2024-incentivizing-quality-text-.tldr: Cost-robust statistical contracts tie text-generation payments to evaluated quality even when a provider's inference costs are unknown.

paragraphs: Trajectory-based offline reinforcement learning uses recorded sequences to learn decision-making behavior. Transformers perform well in this setting, but their size and computational demands motivate alternatives for constrained systems. This paper investigates Decision Mamba, or DeMa, asking which sequence structure and architectural components make Mamba effective for trajectory optimization.

The experiments find that longer sequences add substantial computation without improving DeMa's performance in the studied setting. Its attention to the sequence diminishes approximately exponentially, motivating a Transformer-like design instead of an RNN-like one. The analysis also identifies Mamba's hidden attention mechanism as important to success, reports compatibility with other residual structures, and finds that position embeddings are unnecessary.

The resulting design outperforms Decision Transformer while using 30% fewer parameters on Atari and only one-quarter as many parameters on MuJoCo. These results support Mamba's compatibility with trajectory optimization when its design reflects the observed sequence behavior. The contribution combines an empirical architecture study with a more parameter-efficient model for the tested offline reinforcement-learning tasks.
neurips-2024-is-mamba-compatible-with-tr.tldr: A specially designed Decision Mamba outperforms Decision Transformer on evaluated offline RL tasks with substantially fewer parameters.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning experiments depend on both the learning algorithm and the environments that generate experience. When environments run on CPUs, they can limit the scale of training even when other hardware is available. JaxMARL brings JAX-based hardware acceleration to multi-agent reinforcement learning, combining commonly used environments and popular baseline algorithms in an open-source codebase.

The system enables highly parallel training pipelines and reports wall-clock speedups of up to 12,500 times over existing approaches in its experiments. That maximum is a reported experimental result, rather than a uniform speedup for every workload. Faster execution can make broader and more thorough evaluations feasible, potentially helping address evaluation difficulties in the field.

The paper also introduces SMAX, a simplified, vectorized version of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge. By removing dependence on the StarCraft II game engine, SMAX supports GPU acceleration and offers a more flexible environment. The authors identify self-play and meta-learning among its potential future applications, extending the contribution beyond faster implementations of existing benchmarks.
neurips-2024-jaxmarl-multi-agent-rl-envi.tldr: JaxMARL accelerates multi-agent reinforcement-learning environments and algorithms with JAX and introduces the flexible SMAX benchmark.

paragraphs: Understanding a three-dimensional scene involves individual objects, larger regions, and relationships among them. MMScan organizes language annotations around this hierarchy, addressing the narrower emphasis on object properties and spatial relationships in earlier datasets. Its descriptions move from regions to objects and from single targets to relationships, covering both attributes and spatial understanding.

The dataset builds on existing 3D scans. Vision-language models generate initial annotations through carefully designed prompts, and people correct them for accuracy, naturalness, and coverage. The resulting collection contains 1.4 million meta-annotated captions covering 109,000 objects and 7,700 regions, plus more than 3.04 million samples for 3D visual grounding and question answering.

The authors evaluate representative models to examine their capabilities across different aspects of scene understanding. They also use MMScan to train 3D grounding models and language models, reporting substantial improvements on existing benchmarks and in-the-wild evaluations. The contribution is therefore both an evaluation resource and a training resource, with language tied to scene structure at multiple levels of detail.
neurips-2024-mmscan-a-multi-modal-3d-sce.tldr: MMScan provides hierarchical language annotations for 3D scenes and improves evaluated grounding and language models when used for training.

paragraphs: Noisy Ostracods turns the practical work of building a clean biological taxonomy dataset into a machine-learning benchmark. It contains 71,466 crustacean specimens annotated by specialists for genus and species classification. An estimated 5.58% of genus-level annotations are potentially problematic, making label reliability a central part of the recognition task.

The errors come from several sources. Some specimens belong to classes discovered during curation that were absent from the original labels. Others were assigned to supposed new classes even though they belong to existing ones. The dataset also has extremely uneven class frequencies, with a reported imbalance factor of 22,429, combining rare categories with subtle visual distinctions and varied annotation problems.

Initial experiments find no significant improvement from the tested robust-learning methods over cross-entropy training on the noisy data. Tested noise detectors also identify errors less effectively, by error hit rate, than simple cross-validation ensembling. These findings make the dataset a demanding evaluation resource for methods intended to handle complex, naturally occurring label noise.
neurips-2024-noisy-ostracods-a-fine-grai.tldr: Noisy Ostracods exposes difficulties for existing noise-robust learning methods through fine-grained categories, extreme imbalance, and real annotation errors.

paragraphs: Many selection problems ask for a useful subset while restricting how many items may be chosen. Submodular objectives capture diminishing returns: an item's extra contribution can shrink as the selected set grows. In the non-monotone case considered here, adding items does not always improve the objective, making good selection more challenging.

The paper addresses the tradeoff between a provable approximation guarantee and practical computational effort. It presents an algorithm with a 0.385 approximation guarantee under a cardinality constraint and query complexity O(n + k²). The abstract contrasts this with a stronger 0.401 guarantee from an algorithm described as impractical, and the 1/e guarantees of the best practical alternatives.

The new result improves the stated guarantee available with practical query complexity, without claiming the strongest approximation ratio overall. Evaluations on machine-learning applications, including movie recommendation and image summarization, demonstrate the method's effectiveness. Its contribution is a combination of theoretical solution quality and manageable evaluation cost for constrained subset-selection problems.
neurips-2024-practical-0-385-approximati.tldr: A new subset-selection algorithm combines a 0.385 approximation guarantee with practical O(n + k²) query complexity.

paragraphs: Predicting what a reinforcement-learning agent will do could help people coordinate with it and anticipate dangerous outcomes. This paper experimentally compares prediction for agents that plan explicitly, plan implicitly, or do not plan. It examines both the agent's future actions and events that may occur during deployment.

The study contrasts two sources of predictive information. An inner-state approach reads computations within the agent, such as explicit plans or neuron activations. A simulation approach runs the agent forward inside a learned model of the world. The comparison asks whether useful foresight comes more effectively from the agent's current internal computations or from simulating its future behavior.

Explicit plans are significantly more informative in the reported experiments than the neuron activations of the other agent types. For action prediction, using plans is also more robust to model quality than simulation-based prediction. Event-prediction results are more mixed. The findings therefore distinguish predicting an agent's choices from predicting surrounding events, while supporting the usefulness of both internal information and simulation.
neurips-2024-predicting-future-actions-o.tldr: Explicit agent plans improve future-action prediction in experiments, while comparisons for event prediction yield more mixed results.

paragraphs: Recognizing a particular region within an unconstrained image requires knowing both where something is and what it means. RegionSpot combines pretrained models that specialize in these complementary capabilities. A localization foundation model, such as SAM, supplies position-aware information, while a vision-language model, such as CLIP, supplies semantic knowledge.

Both foundation models remain frozen during training. Optimization focuses on a lightweight attention-based module that integrates their knowledge. This design aims to reuse existing capabilities while reducing training overhead, addressing the expensive training, data-noise sensitivity, and lack of context associated with earlier approaches to region recognition.

Experiments report gains in open-world recognition alongside computational savings, including training with 3 million examples in one day on eight V100 GPUs. RegionSpot exceeds GLIP-L by 2.9 mAP on LVIS validation and by 13.1 AP for rare categories, with a 2.5 AP improvement on ODinW. It also surpasses GroundingDINO-L by 11.0 AP for rare categories on LVIS minival, highlighting the reported benefits for difficult, less common categories.
neurips-2024-recognize-any-regions-a3052.tldr: RegionSpot combines frozen localization and vision-language models through lightweight attention to improve efficient open-world region recognition.

paragraphs: Sharpness-aware minimization, or SAM, can improve how well neural networks generalize, but each update requires two gradient computations performed in sequence. This makes an iteration roughly twice as costly as one using a base optimizer such as stochastic gradient descent. SAMPa modifies SAM so that these two computations can run fully in parallel.

The resulting twofold speedup assumes that communication between devices has negligible cost. That condition matters because the acceleration depends on executing work simultaneously without substantial coordination overhead. Empirically, SAMPa ranks among the most time-efficient SAM variants and consistently outperforms SAM across the vision and language tasks evaluated.

The paper also establishes convergence guarantees when perturbation sizes remain fixed, using a newly developed Lyapunov function. The authors treated that guarantee as a design requirement in deriving the method. SAMPa therefore links an implementation benefit with a theoretical property: its update structure supports parallel computation while retaining the stated convergence behavior, rather than relying only on observed training performance.
neurips-2024-sampa-sharpness-aware-minim.tldr: SAMPa parallelizes SAM's two gradient computations, enabling a twofold speedup when communication costs are negligible while retaining convergence guarantees.

paragraphs: Conversational human videos require facial movement and hand gestures to look convincing at the same time. ShowMaker targets this combination in half-body videos, addressing the difficulty of directly applying methods centered on either facial animation or full-body animation. Its framework uses dual-stream diffusion models with dedicated components for the face and hands.

Hand generation is challenging because the motion guidance is sparse. ShowMaker strengthens positional information from hand key points and constructs a corresponding codebook to support detailed hand modeling. For the face, a separate recapture module extracts texture information and overall identity features from an aligned face, then incorporates those features into diffusion-based generation.

These components give crucial local regions more specific treatment within the overall video model. Quantitative and qualitative experiments report superior visual quality and consistency over time. The findings support the paper's central design choice: explicitly modeling hand structure and facial appearance can improve conversational video generation, where both detailed appearance and coherent motion contribute to the result.
neurips-2024-showmaker-creating-high-fid.tldr: ShowMaker adds specialized hand and face modeling to diffusion models for higher-quality, temporally consistent half-body conversational videos.

paragraphs: Strong performance on general language tasks does not fully describe a model's command of Chinese classical literature and language arts. WenMind provides a dedicated benchmark for this domain, covering ancient prose, ancient poetry, and ancient literary culture. It is intended to broaden evaluation beyond the limited task coverage of earlier benchmarks.

The benchmark contains 4,875 question-answer pairs across 42 detailed tasks and three question formats. It supports two evaluation scenarios, organized around domains and capabilities. The authors use it to assess 31 representative language models, including general-purpose systems and models specifically focused on ancient Chinese, enabling comparisons within a shared evaluation framework.

The best-performing evaluated model, ERNIE-4.0, receives a total score of 64.3, which the authors interpret as leaving substantial room for improvement. Their analysis also identifies model strengths and weaknesses and emphasizes the importance of pretraining data. WenMind contributes a standardized way to study those differences and to assess progress across the distinct areas of classical Chinese knowledge and language ability.
neurips-2024-wenmind-a-comprehensive-ben.tldr: WenMind evaluates 31 language models across Chinese classical literature tasks and finds substantial room for improvement.
